newsitem.title: INDIA: Mandela says Malaysia telecom deal in final stage.
newsitem.headline: Mandela says Malaysia telecom deal in final stage.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Friday that a strategic equity partnership between South Africa's state-owned Telkom and a Malaysian-U.S. consortium had reached the final stages of negotiations.
Telekom Malaysia Bhd and U.S.-based SBC Communications Inc are teaming up to take a joint 30 percent stake in Telkom for a total of $1.26 billion.

"We are proceeding steadily with a restructuring of our state assets -- the acquisition of a strategic equity partner for our national telecommunications agency is in the final stages of negotiations with a Malaysian-United States based consortium," Mandela told a meeting of Indian businessmen in New Delhi.
He added: "And there will be further announcements this year in transport, forestry and the leisure industry."

Earlier on Friday Malaysian news agency Bernama quoted Telekom chief executive Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali as saying Telekom Malaysia, committed to spending around $500 million for a 12 percent stake in South Africa's Telkom, was ready to invest if required.

"Large projects costing hundreds of millions of rands are under way, changing the shape of our economy and our national and regional infrastructure," Mandela, who was speaking on the second day of a three-day visit, told the meeting.

He said the economy, which grew at 3.1 percent in 1996, has been set by his government "on a more ambitious path to achieve six percent growth by the year 2000 and the creation of 400,000 new jobs a year."

"Economic indicators point to underlying changes of the kind we need for sustained growth and development. We are encouraged in particular by our rapidly strengthening export performance; rising productivity and a powerful surge in fixed investment," he said.
